newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila bourse denies Mondragon suspension.
newsitem.headline: Manila bourse denies Mondragon suspension.

text.p: The Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE) said on Friday trading of gaming firm Mondragon International Philippines Inc shares will not be suspended despite a dispute between Mondragon and the Philippine Amusement and Gaming Corp (Pagcor).
The PSE said in an advisory that it had denied a request by Mondragon for the suspension of trading until the dispute with state-run Pagcor was resolved.

Mondragon was granted a permit by Pagcor in 1995 to operate an unlimited number of casinos at the Clark Special Economic Zone, north of Manila. Pagcor, which also operates a nearby casino, has accused Mondragon of violations of the permit.

"We are well aware that the main reason for the strong showing of Mondragon has been the anticip ated results of our casino operations. Therefore, we seek your consent to the request," Mondragon chairman Jose Antonio Gonzalez told the bourse in a statement.
"With respect to the request for voluntary suspension from trading, the exchange deems it proper to allow the trading of the securities to continue," the PSE said.
